chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Verily, God created happiness and misery before He created His creation. So whoever God created as happy, He will not hate him ever — and even if he commits evil deeds, He hates his deed but does not hate him. And if he was (created as) miserable, God will not love him ever — and even if he performs righteous deeds, He loves his deed but hates him, because of what he will come to. So when God loves something, He will never hate it; and when He hates something, He will never love it.

key_terms.السَّعَادَة: Happiness/felicity (sa'adah) — the state of being divinely favored and destined for a good end; a technical theological term in discussions of predestination
key_terms.الشَّقَاء: Misery/wretchedness (shaqa') — the state of being divinely destined for an ill end; the opposite of sa'adah in theological discourse
key_terms.خَلَقَ خَلْقَهُ: Created His creation — emphasizes that divine decrees predate the existence of creatures
key_terms.سَعِيد: Happy/fortunate one — one predestined by God for felicity
key_terms.شَقِيّ: Wretched/miserable — one predestined for an unfortunate end

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about happiness and misery being created before human beings in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) presents a profound theological statement about divine predestination: God decreed happiness (sa'adah) and misery (shaqa') for His creatures before their very creation. The hadith draws a sharp distinction between God's relationship to a person and His relationship to their deeds — a happy person's evil acts are hated by God while the person is still loved; a miserable person's good acts may be loved while the person is still hated due to their ultimate destiny. This reflects the classical Shia theological doctrine of divine foreknowledge and the immutability of God's will, while also affirming that God's love and hate are eternal and unchanging attributes.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Created ‘السَّعَادَةَ وَ الشَّقَاءَ’ the happiness and the misery before He<sup>azwj</sup> Created His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures. So the one whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Created as happy, He<sup>azwj</sup> would not Hate him ever, and even if he performs evil deeds. He<sup>azwj</sup> would Hate his deed, and would not Hate him.
And if he was (Created) ‘شَقِيّاً’ miserable, He<sup>azwj</sup> would not Love him ever, and even if performed righteous deeds. He<sup>azwj</sup> would Love his deed and Hate him due to what he would be coming to. So when Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Loves something, He<sup>azwj</sup> would not Hate it, ever, and when He<sup>azwj</sup> Hates a thing, He<sup>azwj</sup> would not Love it, ever’.
en.sarwar: 1. It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Saffron ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Allah created good fortune and bad fortune before He created the creatures. Whoever Allah has created fortunate He never becomes angry with him even though he may do bad deeds. He to reach and nor do the deep diving intelligence is capable to grasp. Most High is Allah. It is He who is not subject to the effects of the numbered time or extended period or limited attributes. Glorious is Allah, Who has no beginning that started or a destination that would close or an end that would finish. Glorious is He Who is just as He Him Self has introduced. Those who speak of His attributes can never praise Him duly. He gave to everything a limit at the time of its creation for their non- similarity to Him and His none-similarity to them. For Him th of would dislike his deeds but his own self. If he is an unfortunate He would never love him even if he would do good deeds. He would love his deeds but not his own self because of what he will end up to. If Allah would love someone He will not dislike him and if He would dislike someone He will not love him.”
